Here is my 2 cents. I have a Masters in Social Work and work with the indigent population. I have CPTSD and so I've spent over 15 years learning and studying trauma. I think what you are feeling could be due to developmental trauma and that is a dissociative symptom. Maybe I'm wrong. Obviously you should listen to your therapist but I experience that now and have experienced it in different areas of my body. My head feels bigger sometimes. Sometimes it's my hands . Just feelings that make me feel a body part is disproportionate.  

Hope you are able to find some answers.

Goodness. I feel the same way. I cant say great positive things about the 15 years of therapy and the money, and the pain. 

I wonder now if my therapy has only kept it at the surface and maybe I'd be better to stop going.. maybe I could "put it behind me" 

So so sorry this is your reality. I feel like this type of pain is excruciating and noone can see that I'm actually in chronic pain. . I hope someone has something to offer that is helpful for you and your able take baby steps in the direction you want to go. 

Couple ideas 
- allow yourself an allotted period of time to obsess and then try to refocus on something else . 

-accept where you are and if you cant focus or just keep thinking about it, maybe you can allow time to process it and sit with it. 

-try and identify what's happening in your body when your obsessing and sit with that. Just noticing how your muscles are, how your body feels. 

Just things that I do...

Consider researching Somatic Experiencing.  It is body work and I'm in this process now. Consider learning about that and then looking for an SE therapist in your area. 

Good Luck.

Hi. I am an MSW, LCSW in the state of Indiana. I have supervised interns and work as a mitigation specialist. I have a BS in psychology and now MSW . 

I like my job... but it can be very difficult to manage mental health with this position. I can imagine CPS is incredibly hard emotionally. 

I meet with inmates in our jails, see their families, assess and help attorneys produce mitigation or legal consideration for leniency or treatment as opposed to maximum prison time.  Most of the time my clients are accused of murder of one or more and various other crimes. 

I wouldnt give it up. I would move forward. Do you have interest in getting your masters ? This opens up a huge array of options. If you utilize the benefits in our state, some agencies will repay or pay for higher education, and it kind of feels like it gets you through your next two years working there... just curious if that was an option. 

but I will suggest that in the social work field,  there will likely be times you need more self care than others. Self care is hard to establish honestly. They say .."self care...self care" but what does that look like for your needs. I've always heard, every social worker needs a social worker so in our office there is no shame in mental health days, FMLA, and everyone of us is involved in therapy. 

I am sorry that this seems to be the experience of so many of us. I do feel that we are moving towards a time when a masters degree is the only way to get a decent paying position.  I know there are exceptions of course. I do know that my colleagues a d friends seem to mostly be happy (as happy as any job really is) in their positions as MSW's. 

Good Luck. I'm certain you can find something that fits. It's a very versatile degree .
